newsitem.title: UK: Options-Coffee vols steady, sees forward interest.
newsitem.headline: Options-Coffee vols steady, sees forward interest.

text.p: Volatilities on the coffee options held steady this week but activity was curbed by a see-sawing futures market while white sugar options saw unusually high volume on short strangle deals in May.
Cocoa options were in the doldrums on poor participation as the futures market remained rangebound although the technical picture showed signs of improvement.
In coffee, dealings turned quieter this week after a hectic pace in the past few weeks as operators sought protection on the back of volatile New York-traded arabica coffee futures.
But traders were starting to see growing enquiries far out in the forward July and September months as players tried to build some safeguards against any frost risk.
The Brazilian winter season begins in June. The last frosts in 1994 ravaged many Brazilian plantations.
The Coffee futures market looked like settling down this week when it was stirred on Wednesday by conflicting reports of Colombian crop forecasts.
The benchmark May was driven to a high of $1,635 a tonne and a low of $1,550 on Wednesday. Prices had since fallen back to trade at around $1,580 by late Friday afternoon.
Traders said the market could be consolidating at this level after the frenzied fund-led buying since the start of the year which took values by up to 40-45 percent.
But sentiment remained jittery and the market could swing sharply up if the current nearby supply woes showed signs of worsening.
An options trader said there been enquiries for July and September $2,010 calls.
"There have significant enquiries for out-of-the-money calls. This is the time of the year to buy them and get ready for the frosts," said one.
Volatilities for May $2,00 calls and July and September $2,010 calls were seen at a steep 55 percent.
Otherwise, other May strikes have volatilities of 40 percent and July and September at 44 percent.
An unusually high volume of trades on Wednesday dominated activity on white sugar options this week.
One trade house was reported to have sold a May short strangle combination of $320 calls and $290 puts at a cheap $1.40 premium, in a total volume of 1,200 lots.
On the same day, a session when the May futures contract slumped $2.10 to an intraday low of $304, 900 lots of May $300 calls were also traded.

"There was a large client in the market who had a specific transaction, sold the volatilities lower and consequently people were willing to pick them up," said one trader, adding that various brokers bought the order.
In cocoa, market makers said it would be a good strategy to buy May and July calls in view of their attractive premiums.
"Call options are very, very cheap," said one.
He said in view of the huge net speculative short positions which could be as large as 10,000 lots, there could be a major short-covering move in the coming weeks to push prices sharply higher.
The futures market trended slightly higher but still within an immediate range of 870-890 stg.
Chart-wise, a move this week to 890 stg basis May was seen as technically constructive but the contract needs to close near or above 900 stg for a continued rally.
-- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
